title: Chrysin attenuates dimethoate-induced multi-organ oxidative toxicity in rats: an integrated toxicological and redox biomarker profiling study
content:
Abstract
This research analyzed the protective impact of the natural flavonoid chrysin (CHR) against oxidative damage and biochemical dysfunction affecting multiple organs following exposure to dimethoate (DM), an organophosphorus compound. The investigation used 40 healthy male Wistar albino rats, randomly assigned to four different groups: control, DM (20 mg/kg/day), CHR (80 mg/kg/day), and DM + CHR. All treatments were given orally for twenty-one days. Oxidative variables were evaluated in the liver, kidneys, brain, testis, heart, lungs, and blood. The measured biomarkers included the following: malondialdehyde (MDA), glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px), superoxide dismutase (SOD), glutathione reductase (GR), glutathione S-transferase (GST), catalase (CAT), glutathione (GSH) and several blood biochemical parameters. Principal component analysis and heatmap analysis were also performed to assess the overall redox-stressed system. DM administration elevated tissue lipid peroxidation, decreased GSH levels and antioxidant enzyme activities, and changed serum biochemical parameters, demonstrating a systemic oxidative stress reaction involving multiple organs. CHR by itself failed to significantly affect the evaluated parameters, while CHR co-treatment slightly improved DM-induced oxidative and biochemical changes. Multivariate analyses demonstrated that DM exposure produced a different systemic redox profile, while CHR shifted this profile toward the control structure. Overall, this research adds to the literature with a comprehensive multi-organ and multivariate evaluation of DM-induced redox imbalance and demonstrating the biomarker-level protective effect of CHR against pesticide-induced oxidative toxicity. Further histopathological and molecular investigations are needed to verify these effects and clarify underlying mechanisms in tissues impacted and circulating blood.
